title: `project_file_unwritable` can claim nothing changed after an earlier write landed
description: Found while fixing WCLI-7 (the review's F4 class, one step further out). src/contract/errors.ts declares project_file_unwritable as 'Ward could not read or write a project file. Nothing was changed.' A single-target run makes that true, but ward init writes the manifest and then each selected bridge file, and the write of a later target can fail (unwritable or read-only file, a write error) after an earlier one has landed via temp-file-and-rename. The error then reports that nothing was changed while a file in the repository has, in fact, changed. Not fixed in WCLI-7 because it changes a user-facing contract string outside that task's review fix list; recorded here rather than left silent. Related and deliberately NOT in scope: whether the fix is a truthful rewording or a reordering is a design decision, and the same question applies to any multi-file command that reports a single 'nothing changed' claim.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The message a failed multi-file write reports is true in every path that raises it: a test makes the second of two targets unwritable after the first has been written, and asserts the reported text does not claim that nothing was changed (and documents what it does claim)

No other error in the catalog carries an unqualified nothing-was-changed claim in a path that can follow a successful write; each is either verified single-target or reworded, and the audit is recorded in the task notes

plan: 2. Contract: reword project_file_unwritable to "Ward could not read or write a project file. Ward did not change it." and vault_busy to "Another Ward process held the vault for too long. The vault was not changed." (DEC-10 Option A, accepted; the first sentence is unchanged, only the unqualified reassurance is scoped).

3. Test (AC1): in project-binding.test.ts, make the checkout root read-only with .ward writable so the manifest lands and the CLAUDE.md write fails; assert exit 4, code project_file_unwritable, the manifest changed on disk, and the reported text scoped to a project file rather than claiming nothing changed.
4. Audit (AC2): record the per-entry verdicts for the five catalog entries carrying the claim, with the raise sites and write ordering that make each true.
5. Records and gates: task notes for the DEC-10 reading and the audit; bun run check; lore check --strict; independent review over the diff; PR into dev with CI green; merge bare, then promote.
implementationNotes:
WCLI-27 IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-29, branch feat/WCLI-27-honest-nothing-changed). DESIGN SOURCE READ FIRST-PARTY, not relayed: DEC-10 at opum-ai/opum-agent origin/main, .quest/planning.json decisions[9], status accepted, outcome "ACCEPTED: OPTION A, REWORD, as the packet scopes it. ... The approved strings: project_file_unwritable becomes 'Ward could not read or write a project file. Ward did not change it.' and vault_busy becomes 'The vault was not changed.' NOT AUTHORISED: the variant 'A plus a separate no-partial-write task'." That variant is not filed, and no reorder or no-partial-write work is in this change.

A READING OF DEC-10, STATED BECAUSE THE RECORD ADMITS TWO. The outcome quotes vault_busy's replacement as the reassurance alone ("The vault was not changed.") where it quotes project_file_unwritable's as a whole message. I took the narrower change: the diagnostic sentence "Another Ward process held the vault for too long." is kept and only the unqualified reassurance is replaced. Reasons, in order: (1) minimal change -- the other reading DELETES existing text, which would itself be a change beyond the two approved strings, and DEC-10's own scope clause binds this approval to the option text as written; (2) DEC-10 names the catalog's existing house style as the model, and every sibling entry is a diagnostic plus a scoped claim (vault_store_unrecognized, project_path_unsafe, project_manifest_malformed); (3) vault_busy's own hint, "Retry once the other Ward command has finished", names a cause that only the kept sentence states. If the intent was the wholesale replacement, the difference is one sentence on one line.

WHAT SHIPPED. src/contract/errors.ts: project_file_unwritable now reads "Ward could not read or write a project file. Ward did not change it." and vault_busy now reads "Another Ward process held the vault for too long. The vault was not changed." Each carries a comment naming the write path that made the old claim false. No error type, code, hint or envelope shape changed, so exit codes are untouched.

AC1 MEASURED TWICE, AND THE PAIR IS THE EVIDENCE. test/project-binding.test.ts gains a describe, "WCLI-27: a failed write reports a claim scoped to the file it failed on", holding one test. The scenario is the one WCLI-27 names: the checkout root is chmod 0555 with .ward writable, so the manifest lands and the CLAUDE.md write that follows it fails. FIXED TREE: 32 pass, 0 fail on the file; bun run check exits 0 with 426 pass, 0 fail, 2164 expect() calls across 18 files. PRE-FIX TREE, same invocation, errors.ts stashed: 31 pass, 1 fail, and the only failure is this test's message assertion -- "Expected to contain: 'Ward did not change it.' / Received: 'Ward could not read or write a project file. Nothing was changed.'". The premise assertions (the manifest exists on disk, CLAUDE.md does not) passed on BOTH trees, which is what localises the red to the string rather than to the scenario or the harness: the pre-fix code really does let the manifest land and then report that nothing was changed. The test asserts the premise as well as the text for the same reason -- a message-only assertion would still pass if the write order changed later and the string became true for a different reason.

GATES. bun run check exit 0 (typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check 36 files 0 violations, 426 tests). lore check --strict exit 0, 11 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Both measured on this branch before the PR opened. CI results are on the PR, not claimed here.

AC2 AUDIT, per catalog entry carrying an unqualified nothing-was-changed claim. Five entries carried the exact string "Nothing was changed" at this branch's base, 99880fa (grep src/contract/errors.ts). Two are false in the sense WCLI-27 names and are the two DEC-10 rewords; three are clean and are deliberately left alone. Each verdict is given with the raise sites and the write ordering that decide it, so a later reader can re-derive it rather than trust it.

FALSE, REWORDED. (1) project_file_unwritable -- raise sites src/adapters/project-files.ts:57, :178, :214, :243. The one that can follow a landed write is :214 in atomicWrite, reached from src/application/project.ts:230-233, which writes the manifest and then each selected bridge file in target order, so a later target failing leaves the manifest already renamed into place. (2) vault_busy -- raise site src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts:253. Two paths reach it after a write: src/application/project.ts:307-311 prepares, and therefore writes, the project files before :320 registerForProject's store.mutate can raise it; and src/application/backup.ts:179 stores the key before :180 store.create can raise it. The vault transaction itself rolls back, which is why the reword narrows the claim to the vault instead of dropping it.

CLEAN, VERIFIED SINGLE-TARGET, NOT REWORDED. (3) setup_in_progress -- raise sites src/adapters/setup-session.ts:114, :141, :152, :237, all inside lock acquisition. src/cli/main.ts:101 makes acquireSetupSession the first statement of setupCommand, before the store or the key provider is constructed. The only write that can precede it is setup-session.ts:189 prepareVaultDirectory, which creates the directory only when it is absent -- and every raise site requires a lock file INSIDE that same directory to exist, so in every path that raises, the directory already existed before this run touched anything. (4) backup_malformed -- reachable only through parseBackup (src/domain/backup.ts:311, with decodeBase64 at :301 and :307 and ownRecord beneath it) and openBackup (:252), and those are called only at src/application/backup.ts:167 and :169, both before the first write at :179. runBackup parses no backup: it calls sealBackup and encodeBackup and writes last, at src/application/backup.ts:116-117. (5) backup_open_failed -- one raise site, src/domain/backup.ts:266 inside openBackup, reached only from src/application/backup.ts:169, again before the first write at :179.

COVERAGE, stated because it is the part that does not travel with the verdicts. This audit is over the string "Nothing was changed", which is the claim WCLI-27 names. It is NOT an audit of every claim that a change did not happen: vault_store_unrecognized, project_manifest_malformed, project_path_unsafe, instructions_markers_conflict and others say "Ward did not change it" and were not re-checked here. They were out of this task's scope by its own wording, and none of them is known to be false -- but none of them is verified here either, and the next reader should not read this note as clearing them.

NO BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Before the change, no test, doc, fixture or script pinned any of the five strings: grep over src, test, docs and scripts for the claim and for both rewordings returns nothing outside src/contract/errors.ts, which is why the two edits broke no test. The only file that quotes the old text afterwards is WCLI-27's own description, which is a record of the finding and is left as written rather than rewritten to match the fix.
